subject: GOF tests when no degrees of freedom

messages.author: f9dee1336056abf1
messages.subject: GOF tests when no degrees of freedom
parts:
Hi all,

Just a quick question about the best course of action when I have no degrees of freedom, and therefore cannot perform gof tests.

ds() has selected a half-normal function with cosine(2,3,4) adjustments as this has the lowest AIC value, but the result of this is that there are no degrees of freedom for the gof test.

What is the best option in this case?

Many thanks in advance,

Oscar

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] GOF tests when no degrees of freedom
parts:
Oscar

Seems your model has quite a few adjustment terms.  One "ad hoc" approach might be to force the fit of a model with sufficiently few adjustment terms such that a GOF test has degrees of freedom to produce a test result.  If that GOF test (with few adjustments) shows adequate fit, then it seems probable that a model with more adjustments would fit even better.

Alternatively, you may need to resort to visual assessment of fit, rather than quantitative.  That is the challenge presented by binned data--there is less information available to assess fit.
